concepts.title: Central Problems and Types of Economies
concepts.description: Central Problems and Types of Economies — part of the chapter on Introduction to Microeconomics.
key_ideas: Core principles of central problems and types of economies
Step-by-step problem solving for central problems and types of economies
Real-world applications of central problems and types of economies

concepts.title: Microeconomics vs Macroeconomics
concepts.description: Differentiation between the two main branches of economics based on the scope of study, variables used, and the level of aggregation.
key_ideas: Study of individual units (household/firm) vs. economy as a whole
Price theory vs. Income and Employment theory
Partial equilibrium vs. General equilibrium analysis

concepts.title: Positive and Normative Economics
concepts.description: Analysis of the distinction between objective economic statements based on facts and subjective statements based on value judgments.
key_ideas: Positive economics: 'What is' (verifiable facts)
Normative economics: 'What ought to be' (opinions/suggestions)
Role of value judgments in economic policy

concepts.title: Opportunity Cost
concepts.description: Understanding the cost of a decision in terms of the next best alternative foregone due to scarce resources.
key_ideas: Value of the next best alternative foregone
Relationship between scarcity, choice, and cost
Application in decision making for individuals and nations

concepts.title: Production Possibility Frontier (PPF)
concepts.description: Graphical representation showing the possible combinations of two goods that an economy can produce with given resources and technology.
key_ideas: Attainable vs. unattainable combinations
Efficient vs. inefficient utilization of resources
Shift vs. rotation of the PPC

concepts.title: Marginal Rate of Transformation (MRT)
concepts.description: Examination of the rate at which one good must be sacrificed to produce an additional unit of another good, determining the shape of the PPF.
key_ideas: Slope of the Production Possibility Curve
Law of Increasing Marginal Opportunity Cost
Concave shape of the PPC relative to the origin

chapters.title: Theory of Consumer Behaviour / Demand and Supply

concepts.title: Demand, Supply Curves and Equilibrium
concepts.description: Demand, Supply Curves and Equilibrium — part of the chapter on Theory of Consumer Behaviour / Demand and Supply.
key_ideas: Core principles of demand, supply curves and equilibrium
Step-by-step problem solving for demand, supply curves and equilibrium
Real-world applications of demand, supply curves and equilibrium

concepts.title: Cardinal Utility Analysis
concepts.description: Introduction to consumer behavior through the cardinal utility approach, focusing on how consumers measure satisfaction and the psychological law governing consumption.
key_ideas: Total Utility (TU) vs. Marginal Utility (MU)
Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility
Relationship between TU and MU curves

concepts.title: Ordinal Utility: Indifference Curve Analysis
concepts.description: Analysis of consumer preferences using the ordinal approach, examining how consumers choose combinations of two goods given a budget constraint.
key_ideas: Properties of Indifference Curves (convexity, non-intersection)
Marginal Rate of Substitution (MRS)
Budget Line and Budget Set
Conditions for Consumer Equilibrium (Tangency point)

concepts.title: Movements along vs. Shifts in Curves
concepts.description: Distinguishing between changes in quantity demanded/supplied (caused by own price) and changes in demand/supply (caused by other factors).
key_ideas: Expansion and Contraction of Demand/Supply
Increase and Decrease (Shifts) in Demand/Supply
Impact of determinants like income, taste, and related goods prices

concepts.title: Price Elasticity of Demand
concepts.description: Measurement of the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price, including calculation methods and degrees of elasticity.
key_ideas: Percentage Method of calculation
Degrees of elasticity (Perfectly elastic to Perfectly inelastic)
Factors affecting price elasticity of demand
Relationship between Expenditure and Elasticity

concepts.title: Price Elasticity of Supply
concepts.description: Quantifying how quantity supplied responds to changes in the price of the good, focusing on the geometric and percentage methods.
key_ideas: Calculation of supply elasticity
Geometric method (supply curve intercept)
Time horizons (Short run vs. Long run elasticity)
Factors influencing supply elasticity

concepts.title: Production Function and Cost Curves
concepts.description: Production Function and Cost Curves — part of the chapter on Production and Costs.
key_ideas: Core principles of production function and cost curves
Step-by-step problem solving for production function and cost curves
Real-world applications of production function and cost curves

concepts.title: Total, Average, and Marginal Product
concepts.description: Definitions and mathematical relationships between Total Product (TP), Average Product (AP), and Marginal Product (MP) of an input.
key_ideas: Total Product is the sum total of output produced by all units of a variable factor.
Average Product is output per unit of variable input (TP/L).
Marginal Product is the change in output resulting from employing one additional unit of variable input.

concepts.title: The Law of Variable Proportions
concepts.description: Analysis of the short-run production behavior where one factor varies while others remain fixed, focusing on the three stages of production.
key_ideas: Stage 1 (Increasing Returns): MP increases and TP increases at an increasing rate.
Stage 2 (Diminishing Returns): MP falls but is positive; TP increases at a decreasing rate.
Stage 3 (Negative Returns): MP becomes negative and TP starts falling.

concepts.title: Returns to Scale (Long Run)
concepts.description: Examination of how output responds to a proportional increase in all inputs simultaneously in the long run.
key_ideas: Increasing Returns to Scale (IRS): Output increases by a larger proportion than inputs.
Constant Returns to Scale (CRS): Output increases by the same proportion as inputs.
Decreasing Returns to Scale (DRS): Output increases by a smaller proportion than inputs.

concepts.title: Short Run Costs: Fixed and Variable
concepts.description: Differentiation between fixed costs (which do not change with output) and variable costs (which change directly with output) in the short run.
key_ideas: Total Fixed Cost (TFC) remains horizontal/constant regardless of output level.
Total Variable Cost (TVC) starts from origin and increases with output (inverse S-shape).
Total Cost (TC) is the summation of TFC and TVC.

concepts.title: Average and Marginal Cost Relationships
concepts.description: Graphical and theoretical analysis of the geometric shapes of Average Cost (AC), Average Variable Cost (AVC), and Marginal Cost (MC) curves.
key_ideas: AC and AVC curves are U-shaped due to the Law of Variable Proportions.
The MC curve cuts both the AC and AVC curves at their respective minimum points.
The vertical distance between AC and AVC represents Average Fixed Cost (AFC), which diminishes as output rises.

concepts.title: Price and Output Determination
concepts.description: Price and Output Determination — part of the chapter on Market Forms — Perfect Competition, Monopoly.
key_ideas: Core principles of price and output determination
Step-by-step problem solving for price and output determination
Real-world applications of price and output determination

concepts.title: Features of Perfect Competition
concepts.description: An introduction to the theoretical market structure characterized by a large number of buyers and sellers dealing in homogeneous products.
key_ideas: Large number of buyers and sellers ensuring no individual influence on price
Homogeneous products leading to perfect substitution
Free entry and exit of firms in the long run
Firms act as 'Price Takers' rather than 'Price Makers'

concepts.title: Monopoly Market Structure
concepts.description: Analysis of a market structure dominated by a single seller with full control over supply and price.
key_ideas: Single seller and large number of buyers
Absence of close substitutes for the product
Strong barriers to entry for new firms
Firm acts as a 'Price Maker'

concepts.title: Monopolistic Competition
concepts.description: Examination of a market structure that blends elements of monopoly and perfect competition, common in real-world retail.
key_ideas: Large number of sellers selling differentiated products
Product differentiation based on brand, quality, or design
Existence of selling costs (advertisement expenses)
Freedom of entry and exit

concepts.title: Oligopoly and Interdependence
concepts.description: Study of a market structure characterized by a few large firms and high strategic interdependence.
key_ideas: Few large sellers dominate the market
High degree of interdependence in decision-making
Formation of cartels or collusive behaviors
Rigid prices and non-price competition

concepts.title: Revenue Curves in Different Markets
concepts.description: Comparative analysis of how Average Revenue (AR) and Marginal Revenue (MR) curves behave under different market forms.
key_ideas: AR and MR are horizontal and equal in Perfect Competition
AR and MR are downward sloping in Monopoly and Monopolistic Competition
MR falls twice as fast as AR in linear demand monopoly models
Elasticity of demand determines the steepness of the revenue curves

concepts.title: GDP and Methods of Calculation
concepts.description: GDP and Methods of Calculation — part of the chapter on National Income Accounting.
key_ideas: Core principles of gdp and methods of calculation
Step-by-step problem solving for gdp and methods of calculation
Real-world applications of gdp and methods of calculation

concepts.title: Basic Concepts of Macroeconomics
concepts.description: Foundational classification of goods and economic variables essential for understanding national income accounting.
key_ideas: Distinction between final goods and intermediate goods
Consumption goods vs. capital goods
Difference between stock variables (point of time) and flow variables (period of time)

concepts.title: Circular Flow of Income
concepts.description: The continuous flow of goods, services, and money between different sectors of the economy, focusing on the two-sector model.
key_ideas: Real flow (goods/services) vs. Money flow
Phases: Generation, Distribution, and Disposition
Circular flow in a simple two-sector economy (Households and Firms)

concepts.title: Related Aggregates of National Income
concepts.description: Techniques to derive various national income aggregates (GNP, NNP, NDP) from GDP using specific economic adjustments.
key_ideas: Gross vs. Net: Adjustment for Depreciation (Consumption of Fixed Capital)
Domestic vs. National: Adjustment for Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)
Market Price vs. Factor Cost: Adjustment for Net Indirect Taxes

concepts.title: Real vs. Nominal GDP
concepts.description: Differentiation between GDP valued at current prices versus constant prices to assess true economic growth.
key_ideas: Nominal GDP (Current Prices) vs. Real GDP (Base Year Prices)
The concept and calculation of the GDP Deflator
Impact of inflation on economic measurement

concepts.title: GDP and Economic Welfare
concepts.description: Critical assessment of GDP as an index of social welfare and its inherent limitations.
key_ideas: Positive and negative externalities
Non-monetary exchanges (barter, household work)
Distribution of income (inequality) and composition of GDP

concepts.title: Money Supply, RBI and Credit Creation
concepts.description: Money Supply, RBI and Credit Creation — part of the chapter on Money and Banking.
key_ideas: Core principles of money supply, rbi and credit creation
Step-by-step problem solving for money supply, rbi and credit creation
Real-world applications of money supply, rbi and credit creation

concepts.title: Barter System and Functions of Money
concepts.description: Explains the historical evolution of money from the barter system, highlighting the limitations of direct exchange and how money addresses these issues through its specific functional roles.
key_ideas: Limitations of Barter System (Double Coincidence of Wants)
Money as a Medium of Exchange
Money as a Unit of Account and Measure of Value
Standard of Deferred Payment and Store of Value

concepts.title: Demand for Money: Liquidity Preference
concepts.description: Analyzes the motives behind why individuals and firms choose to hold liquid cash, focusing on the relationship between income, interest rates, and the demand for money.
key_ideas: Transaction Motive (Relationship with Income)
Speculative Motive (Relationship with Interest Rates)
The Liquidity Trap
Velocity of Circulation

concepts.title: Instruments of Monetary Policy
concepts.description: Examines the specific quantitative and qualitative tools employed by the Central Bank (RBI) to regulate the money supply and availability of credit in the economy to achieve stability.
key_ideas: Legal Reserve Requirements (CRR and SLR)
Policy Rates (Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, Bank Rate)
Open Market Operations (OMO)
Qualitative Instruments (Margin Requirements, Moral Suasion)

concepts.title: Fiscal Policy, Revenue, Expenditure
concepts.description: Fiscal Policy, Revenue, Expenditure — part of the chapter on Government Budget and the Economy.
key_ideas: Core principles of fiscal policy, revenue, expenditure
Step-by-step problem solving for fiscal policy, revenue, expenditure
Real-world applications of fiscal policy, revenue, expenditure

concepts.title: Objectives of Government Budget
concepts.description: Exploration of the core purposes served by the government budget, focusing on how it influences economic stability and social welfare.
key_ideas: Reallocation of resources based on social and economic priorities
Reduction of inequalities in income and wealth through taxes and subsidies
Economic stability and management of inflationary or deflationary gaps
Management of public enterprises

concepts.title: Classification of Budget Receipts
concepts.description: Differentiation between revenue receipts (tax and non-tax) and capital receipts based on liability creation and asset reduction.
key_ideas: Revenue Receipts: Do not create liability or reduce assets (e.g., Tax, Fees)
Capital Receipts: Create liability or reduce assets (e.g., Borrowings, Disinvestment)
Distinction between Direct Taxes (incidence cannot be shifted) and Indirect Taxes (incidence can be shifted)

concepts.title: Classification of Budget Expenditure
concepts.description: Analysis of government spending categorized into revenue expenditure (operational) and capital expenditure (developmental/asset creation).
key_ideas: Revenue Expenditure: Recurring expenses that do not create assets or reduce liabilities (e.g., Salaries, Interest payments)
Capital Expenditure: Spending that creates assets or reduces liabilities (e.g., Infrastructure, Repayment of loans)
Impact of expenditure types on future economic growth

concepts.title: Measures of Government Deficit
concepts.description: Calculation and interpretation of the three major types of budgetary deficits: Revenue, Fiscal, and Primary Deficit.
key_ideas: Revenue Deficit formula: Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Receipts
Fiscal Deficit formula: Total Expenditure - (Revenue Receipts + Non-debt Capital Receipts)
Primary Deficit formula: Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments
Fiscal Deficit as a measure of total borrowing requirements

concepts.title: Implications of Budgetary Deficits
concepts.description: Evaluation of the economic consequences of high government deficits, including the risks of inflation and debt traps.
key_ideas: Inflationary spiral caused by deficit financing (printing money)
The Debt Trap: Borrowing to pay interest on previous loans
Crowding out effect on private investment
Intergenerational equity and the burden on future generations

concepts.title: BOP, Foreign Exchange and Exchange Rate
concepts.description: BOP, Foreign Exchange and Exchange Rate — part of the chapter on Balance of Payments.
key_ideas: Core principles of bop, foreign exchange and exchange rate
Step-by-step problem solving for bop, foreign exchange and exchange rate
Real-world applications of bop, foreign exchange and exchange rate

concepts.title: Current Account of BOP
concepts.description: Explores the component of BOP that records exports and imports of goods and services, and unilateral transfers within a specific time period.
key_ideas: Balance of Trade (Visibles)
Trade in Invisibles (Services)
Unilateral Transfers (Gifts, Remittances)
Current Account Surplus vs. Deficit

concepts.title: Capital Account of BOP
concepts.description: Examines the component of BOP that records all international transactions involving assets, liabilities, and capital transfers, affecting the country's foreign assets and liabilities.
key_ideas: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) and Portfolio Investment (FII)
External Commercial Borrowings and Assistance
Banking Capital and NRI Deposits
Change in Foreign Exchange Reserves

concepts.title: Autonomous and Accommodating Items
concepts.description: Distinguishes between transactions undertaken for economic motives (profit) and transactions undertaken by the central bank to cover BOP deficits or surpluses.
key_ideas: Autonomous Items (Above the Line)
Accommodating Items (Below the Line)
Economic Motive vs. Balancing Motive
Determination of BOP Deficit or Surplus

concepts.title: Foreign Exchange Rate Systems
concepts.description: Compares different regimes used by countries to manage their currency valuation against other currencies.
key_ideas: Fixed Exchange Rate System (Pegged)
Flexible (Floating) Exchange Rate System
Managed Floating (Dirty Floating)
Role of Central Banks in different systems

concepts.title: Determination of Exchange Rate
concepts.description: Analyzes how the equilibrium exchange rate is determined by the forces of demand and supply in a flexible exchange market.
key_ideas: Sources of Demand for Foreign Exchange
Sources of Supply of Foreign Exchange
Equilibrium Rate Determination
Currency Appreciation vs. Depreciation
